questions.text:
Suppose the following functional dependencies hold on a relation U with attributes [latex]P, Q, R, S, \text{ and } T[/latex]:

[latex]P \rightarrow QR \\ RS \rightarrow T[/latex]

Which of the following functional dependencies can be inferred from the above functional dependencies?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]P\rightarrow QR[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]P\rightarrow R[/latex] (decomposition) True
- [latex]PS\rightarrow RS[/latex] (augmentation) and [latex]RS\rightarrow T[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow T[/latex] True
- [latex]P\rightarrow Q[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]PS\rightarrow Q[/latex] True
- [latex]R\rightarrow T[/latex]: [latex]R^+=\{R\}[/latex], so not implied False

Answer: [latex]PS\rightarrow T,\ P\rightarrow R,\ PS\rightarrow Q[/latex]

questions.text:
Let S be the following schedule of operations of three transactions [latex]T_1, T_2 \text{ and }T_3[/latex] in a relational database system:

[latex]R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y)W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)[/latex]

Consider the statements P and Q below:

P: S is conflict-serializable.
Q: If [latex]T_3[/latex] commits before [latex]T_1[/latex] finishes, then S is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Conflicts:
- [latex]R_1(Y)[/latex] before [latex]W_2(Y)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2
- [latex]W_1(X)[/latex] before [latex]R_3(X)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- [latex]R_2(Z)[/latex] before [latex]W_3(Z)[/latex]: T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T1, T2, T3). P is true.

T3 reads X written by T1. If T3 commits before T1, and T1 later aborts, T3 cannot be undone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not recoverable. Q is false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both P and Q are true
P is true and Q is false
P is false and Q is true
Both P and Q are false

questions.text:
The relation scheme given below is used to store information about the employees of a company, where empId is the key and deptId indicates the department to which the employee is assigned. Each employee is assigned to exactly one department.

[latex]\textsf{emp($\underline{\textsf{empId}}$, name, gender, salary, deptId)}[/latex]

Consider the following SQL query:
 select deptId, count(*)
from emp
where gender = "female" and salary > (select avg(salary)from emp)
group by deptId;
The above query gives, for each department in the company, the number of female employees whose salary is greater than the average salary of
questions.solution:
The subquery (select avg(salary) from emp) has no condition and is not correlated, so it is the average salary of all employees in the company.

Answer: employees in the company

questions.text: A data file consisting of 1,50,000 student-records is stored on a hard disk with block size of 4096 bytes. The data file is sorted on the primary key RollNo. The size of a record pointer for this disk is 7 bytes. Each student-record has a candidate key attribute called ANum of size 12 bytes. Suppose an index file with records consisting of two fields, ANum value and the record pointer the corresponding student record, is built and stored on the same disk. Assume that the records of data file and index file are not split across disk blocks. The number of blocks in the index file is ______
questions.solution:
ANum is not the sorting key, so the index must be dense: one entry per record.

Entry size = 12 + 7 = 19 bytes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] entries per block = [latex]\lfloor4096/19\rfloor=215[/latex].
Blocks = [latex]\lceil150000/215\rceil=698[/latex]

Answer: 698

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following statements S1 and S2 about the relational data model:

S1: A relation scheme can have at most one foreign key.
S2: A foreign key in a relation scheme R cannot be used to refer to tuples of R.

Which one of the following choices is correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: a relation can have several foreign keys (e.g. Enrolment(studentId, courseId) refers to two tables) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- S2: a foreign key can refer to the same relation (e.g. Employee.managerId [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Employee.empId) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are false

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both S1 and S2 are true
S1 is true and S2 is false
S1 is false and S2 is true
Both S1 and S2 are false
